title: An offline approach to fNIRS-guided reinforcement learning for robot behavior
abstract: arXiv:2607.14393v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Human-in-the-loop Reinforcement Learning has become a popular approach for training, finetuning, and aligning robot behavior with user preferences. Our paper explores the feasibility of using brain signals via functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to modulate robot learning in simulation. We compare agents trained on passive (observational) versus active (demonstrative) interaction tasks, and test multiple methods for enhancing the RL algorithm with the neural signal, focusing on parameter augmentation in contrast to replacement. We further examine how model granularity and noise affect agent learning. Our results show that this framework is effective. The neural signal improves learning when augmenting trajectory priorities and state-action q-targets. Additionally, the framework learns successfully from offline data, offering a practical alternative for settings where real-time BCI setups are impractical or only limite

translated_title: 一种基于fNIRS引导的离线强化学习方法用于机器人行为
translated_abstract: 人机协同强化学习已成为训练、微调和对齐机器人行为与用户偏好的流行方法。本文探讨了利用功能性近红外光谱（fNIRS）脑信号在仿真中调节机器人学习的可行性。我们比较了在被动（观察性）与主动（示范性）交互任务上训练的智能体，并测试了多种用神经信号增强强化学习算法的方法，重点对比参数增强与替代策略。我们还研究了模型粒度和噪声对智能体学习的影响。结果表明，该框架是有效的。神经信号在增强轨迹优先级和状态-动作Q目标时能改善学习。此外，该框架能成功从离线数据中学习，为实时脑机接口设置不切实际或数据有限的场景提供了一种实用替代方案。
tldr: 本文提出了一种利用fNIRS脑信号离线增强强化学习的方法，通过参数增强（而非替代）有效提升机器人行为学习性能，并适用于无法实时脑机接口的场景。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an offline fNIRS-guided reinforcement learning approach that enhances robot behavior learning via parameter augmentation (rather than replacement), proving effective and practical for settings lacking real-time BCI capabilities.
